name.text: Using Trig ratios to Find the Base (copy)

questiontext.text:
Find the length of the base (adjacent side) of the right-angled triangle.

Give your answer in exact form (do not convert to decimals).


[[jsxgraph]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard('jxgbox', { boundingbox: [-2, 12, 12, -2], axis: false, keepAspectRatio: true, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false }); /* Right-angle triangle coordinates */ const A = board.create('point', [0, 0], {name: '', fixed: true, size: 2}); // right angle const B = board.create('point', [10, 0], {name: '', fixed: true, size: 2}); // bottom right (angle theta) const C = board.create('point', [0, 10], {name: '', fixed: true, size: 2}); // top /* Triangle edges */ board.create('segment', [A, B]); board.create('segment', [A, C]); board.create('segment', [B, C]); /* Right-angle square at A */ board.create('polygon', [ board.create('point', [0, 0], {visible:false}), board.create('point', [1, 0], {visible:false}), board.create('point', [1, 1], {visible:false}), board.create('point', [0, 1], {visible:false}) ], { fillColor: 'white', fillOpacity: 1, borders: {strokeColor: 'black'} }); /* Labels */ board.create('text', [5, -0.5, 'x'], {fontSize: 14}); // base (horizontal) board.create('text', [5, 6, '{#hyp#}'], {fontSize: 14}); // hypotenuse /* Draw angle arc at B */ board.create('angle', [C, B, A], { radius: 1.2, name: '{#theta#}°', fontSize: 14, withLabel: true, strokeWidth: 2, color: 'blue' }); [[/jsxgraph]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

We are given a right-angled triangle with the right angle at the bottom-left, hypotenuse {@hyp@}, and angle {@theta@}° at the bottom-right. We need to find the base (adjacent side) adj.

The adjacent side is related to the hypotenuse using the cosine ratio:

\[ \cos({@theta@}^\circ) = \frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \frac{\text{adj}}{@hyp@} \]

Solving for the adjacent side gives:

\[ \text{adj} = {@hyp@} \cdot \cos({@theta@}^\circ) \]

Evaluate exactly (no decimals):

  • If \( \theta = 30° \): \(\cos 30° = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), so \[ \text{adj} = {@hyp@} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \frac{{@hyp@}\sqrt{3}}{2} \]
  • If \( \theta = 45° \) : \(\cos 45° = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\), so \[ \text{adj} = {@hyp@} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = \frac{{@hyp@}\sqrt{2}}{2} \]
  • If \( \theta = 60° \): \(\cos 60° = \frac{1}{2}\), so \[ \text{adj} = {@hyp@} \cdot \frac{1}{2} = \frac{{@hyp@}}{2} \]
  • For other angles, leave your answer in exact trig form: \[ \text{adj} = {@hyp@} \cdot \cos({@theta@}^\circ) \]

Tips:

  • When the cosine involves a square root, write your final answer as \(\frac{{@hyp@} \sqrt{n}}{2}\).
  • Do not convert to decimals — keep the exact expression.

Example: If the hypotenuse is 8 and angle θ = 30°:

\[ \text{adj} = 8 \cdot \cos 30° = 8 \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 4 \sqrt{3} \]
